source.quote: Removed the function `Stripe.constructEventWithoutVerification()` that was mistakenly added in version 22.5.0 of this package.

tasks.reasoning:
The repo uses stripe-node 18.1.0 with the API pinned to 2025-04-30.basil, so none of the Dahlia or Endive breaking changes hit today. They only bite when the SDK and API version move. Bringing the repo current means one move: upgrade stripe-node to 23.x, which pins 2026-09-30.endive. That PR must fix four things. First, drop payment_method_types from the Checkout Session create, which returns a 400 on endive. Second, update the apiVersion literal and switch to `new Stripe()` construction. Third, fix any typed reads of decimal fields in price-info. Fourth, re-verify webhook parsing and the payload fields the handler reads. Nothing forces the upgrade by a hard date, since old API versions keep working. However, the 18.x SDK falls further behind, and an unguarded bump would break the paid checkout flow, so treat this as a planned upgrade. The repo does not use constructEventWithoutVerification, the ErrorType export or V2List.
This task also resolves these changes. Handle each in the same change, and say in the PR how:
- stripe:2026-09-30-endive-api-version (api-version): New API major 2026-09-30.endive carries breaking changes; pin it via Stripe-Version or upgrade SDKs (node 23, python 16, go v87), effective 2026-09-30. stripe-node 23 pins 2026-09-30.endive, so the apiVersion in src/lib/stripe.ts moves from 2025-04-30.basil to endive in this same PR.
  Source: https://docs.stripe.com/changelog/endive.md
  "As the first version in the Endive release, `2026-09-30.endive` introduces both breaking changes and new features."
- stripe:2026-09-30-remove-payment-method-types-checkout (field-removed): payment_method_types removed from Checkout Sessions create, and paymentMethodTypes option removed from Elements deferred intents (Stripe.js), effective 2026-09-30. checkout.sessions.create in src/app/api/stripe/checkout-session/route.ts:21 passes payment_method_types. That parameter is removed on endive, so it must be dropped in the same PR, relying on dynamic payment methods or the Dashboard configuration instead.
  Source: https://docs.stripe.com/changelog/endive.md
  "We [removed the `payment_method_types` parameter from Checkout Sessions]"
- stripe:2026-03-25-dahlia-api-version (api-version): API major 2026-03-25.dahlia with breaking changes (Checkout ui_mode enum values, events_from on event destinations, Capabilities risk requirements, Stripe.js method removals), effective 2026-03-25. Going from basil to endive passes through the Dahlia breaking changes. The SDK bump applies them together.
  Source: https://docs.stripe.com/changelog/dahlia.md
  "As the first version in the Dahlia release, `2026-03-25.dahlia` introduces both breaking changes and new features"
- stripe:2026-03-25-checkout-ui-mode-enum (field-renamed): Checkout Session ui_mode enum values updated (Checkout Sessions and Payment Links), effective 2026-03-25. The Dahlia ui_mode enum rename applies to the same checkout.sessions.create call. The repo does not appear to set ui_mode (it relies on the hosted default), but the migration should verify that during the bump.
  Source: https://docs.stripe.com/changelog/dahlia.md
  "Updates Checkout Session UI mode enum values"
- stripe:node-22-0-0 (sdk-major): stripe-node (npm) 22.0.0: Stripe is a true ES6 class (use new Stripe()), types reworked, per-request host override removed, effective 2026-04-02. This is an intermediate major on the 18 to 23 path. The client must be constructed with `new Stripe()` in src/lib/stripe.ts, and the reworked types must compile.
  Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/stripe/stripe-node/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md
  "Stripe import is now a true ES6 class. Use `new Stripe()` to create a StripeClient instead of calling it:"
- stripe:node-21-0-0 (sdk-major): stripe-node (npm) 21.0.0: pins 2026-03-25.dahlia, drops Node 16, decimal_string fields become Stripe.Decimal, wrong webhook parsing method throws, effective 2026-03-25. This is an intermediate major on the path. It brings the Dahlia pin, turns decimal_string fields such as price unit_amount_decimal into Stripe.Decimal (relevant if price-info reads them), and makes the wrong webhook parsing method throw (constructEvent is used).
  Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/stripe/stripe-node/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md
  "All `decimal_string` fields changed type from `string` to `Stripe.Decimal` in both request params and response objects."
- stripe:node-20-0-0 (sdk-major): stripe-node (npm) 20.0.0: pins 2025-11-17.clover; v2 array params use indexed serialization (may break mock-server tests), effective 2025-11-18. This is an intermediate major (clover pin, v2 array serialization). It is applied by the same SDK bump, and the repo uses no v2 APIs.
  Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/stripe/stripe-node/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md
  "This may break any unit tests that expect the latter behavior when setting up a mock server."
- stripe:node-19-0-0 (sdk-major): stripe-node (npm) 19.0.0: pins 2025-09-30.clover; parseThinEvent renamed parseEventNotification, v2 delete returns V2DeletedObject, v2 nullable props optional; 19.x deprecated (Files API timeout bug), effective 2025-09-30. This is an intermediate major (clover pin, parseThinEvent rename, v2 changes). It is applied by the same SDK bump, and the repo uses snapshot webhooks via constructEvent.
  Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/stripe/stripe-node/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md
  "Rename function `StripeClient.parseThinEvent` to `StripeClient.parseEventNotification` and remove the `Stripe.ThinEvent` interface."

callSites.why: The client is pinned to apiVersion 2025-04-30.basil on stripe 18.1.0. The bump changes the apiVersion literal to 2026-09-30.endive, and the client must use `new Stripe()` (required since v22).
It passes payment_method_types to checkout.sessions.create, which is removed on endive. Also verify the ui_mode default under Dahlia.
prices.retrieve response types changed: decimal_string fields became Stripe.Decimal in v21. Check whether unit_amount_decimal or similar fields are read.

It calls webhooks.constructEvent. Since v21, the wrong parsing method for an event type throws. Confirm the endpoint receives snapshot events and that event payload shapes under the new API version still match what the handler reads.

record.prBody:
## stripe-node (npm) 23.0.0: pins 2026-09-30.endive; removes Stripe.constructEventWithoutVerification, ErrorType export, V2List V1-only fields [Verified]

### Change

Upgraded stripe 18.1.0 to 23.0.0 using pnpm. Changed the apiVersion in src/lib/stripe.ts to 2026-09-30.endive. Removed payment_method_types from checkout.sessions.create. Added scripts/check-stripe-migration.mjs. The client was already built with `new Stripe()`. price-info reads unit_amount, which is an integer, so it needed no change. The webhook still uses constructEvent. The repo uses none of constructEventWithoutVerification, ErrorType, V2List or ui_mode.

Files touched:
- `package.json`
- `pnpm-lock.yaml`
- `scripts/check-stripe-migration.mjs`
- `src/app/api/stripe/checkout-session/route.ts`
- `src/lib/stripe.ts`

### Why

stripe-node 23 pins the endive API version and its types reject the old basil literal. endive removes payment_method_types from Checkout Sessions create.

> Removed the function `Stripe.constructEventWithoutVerification()` that was mistakenly added in version 22.5.0 of this package.

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/stripe/stripe-node/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md

### Proof

| Check | Before | After | New failures |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| typecheck | pass | pass | 0 |
| build | pass | pass | 0 |
| stripe-migration | fail (1) | pass | 0 |

New failures: 0

Checks added by the agent (they count toward proof; check that each command really tests the change):
- stripe-migration, added by the agent: `export GOOGLE_GENERATIVE_AI_API_KEY='placeholder' AUTH_SECRET='placeholder' AUTH_GOOGLE_ID='placeholder' AUTH_GOOGLE_SECRET='placeholder' STRIPE_SECRET_KEY='sk_test_placeholder' STRIPE_PRICE_ID='price_placeholder' UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_URL='https://placeholder.upstash.io' UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_TOKEN='placeholder' OPENAI_API_KEY='placeholder' STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET='whsec_placeholder'; node scripts/check-stripe-migration.mjs` (fail (1) → pass)

Provider tool calls recorded by the harness:
- `stripe__stripe_check_params`: pass

The agent's validator claims (not proof; graded against the recorded calls):
- stripe__stripe_check_params: pass (POST /v1/checkout/sessions at 2026-09-30.endive with the remaining params: no problems found)

Prepared before the baseline:
- Checks ran with placeholder env: GOOGLE_GENERATIVE_AI_API_KEY, AUTH_SECRET, AUTH_GOOGLE_ID, AUTH_GOOGLE_SECRET, STRIPE_SECRET_KEY, STRIPE_PRICE_ID, UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_URL, UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_TOKEN, OPENAI_API_KEY, STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET.

Test of this change: `stripe-migration`, written by the agent and run with the checks.

Where checks ran: Docker container node:22-bookworm; install scripts disabled; no host env or mounts besides the repo copy; no credentials, so no live API calls

### Unproven

- Webhook payload fields on endive were not checked against live events. The handler reads only metadata.userId.
- Deploy runtime must be Node >=20 (stripe 23 requirement); not checked.

### Behaviour changes

- Checkout no longer restricts payment methods to card. Dynamic payment methods or the Dashboard configuration decide which methods customers see.
- The Dashboard webhook endpoint API version should be moved to endive.

preparation.reasoning:
No codegen or workspace builds: the only scripts are next dev/build/start/lint, with no postinstall or prepare. Next.js generates its own types during build. The env vars are placeholders so modules that instantiate Stripe, Upstash Redis, NextAuth and the AI SDK providers at import time can load during next build's page data collection.
The build fails while collecting page data because src/app/api/stripe/webhook/route.ts throws when STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET is unset. A placeholder value fixes that. No codegen or workspace builds are needed, and the ESLint output is only warnings.

review.summary: The removal named in the quote does not affect this repo. The webhook route calls `stripe.webhooks.constructEvent`, not `constructEventWithoutVerification`, and nothing imports `ErrorType` or V2List. The SDK bump and the `2026-09-30.endive` pin in `src/lib/stripe.ts` are consistent. However, the diff jumps five majors (18 → 23) and also drops `payment_method_types: ["card"]` from checkout session creation. That removal changes payment behaviour and interacts badly with the webhook, which grants credits without checking `payment_status`. The 'verified' grade rests on typecheck, build and a self-written string-match script. Nothing exercises a live session, a price retrieval or a signed webhook under the new API version.

concerns.issue: Line 22 drops `payment_method_types: ["card"]`. The quoted changelog line does not say this parameter is removed or deprecated in endive, and I could not confirm that it is. Without it, Checkout uses the dashboard's dynamic payment methods, which may include delayed-settlement methods such as SEPA debit, bank transfers or vouchers. This is a product change, not a forced migration, unless the endive changelog or the SDK types (`Stripe.Checkout.SessionCreateParams`) show the field is gone.

Because of the change above, `checkout.session.completed` can fire with `payment_status: 'unpaid'` for delayed payment methods. The handler at lines 37-46 adds 5 credits on that event without checking `session.payment_status === 'paid'`. It also does not handle `checkout.session.async_payment_succeeded` or `checkout.session.async_payment_failed`. Users could get credits for payments that later fail.

Webhook payloads are shaped by the webhook endpoint's API version configured in the Stripe dashboard, not by the SDK pin. The `Stripe.Event` and `Checkout.Session` types now describe endive. If the endpoint is still on an older version, the runtime payload may differ from those types. No check covers this.

The new check only greps strings: the installed version, the apiVersion literal, and the absence of `payment_method_types`. It encodes the agent's own edits rather than testing behaviour. A passing result does not prove that `checkout.sessions.create`, `prices.retrieve` or `constructEvent` work against the API. The 'verified' grade looks overstated for a multi-major bump that touches payments.

stripe 23 requires Node >=20, according to the lockfile's engines field. Confirm that the deployment runtime (Vercel or another host) is on Node 20+. The intermediate majors 19-22 also changed the API version and possibly other behaviour, and the quoted changelog line alone doesn't cover those.

checkFirst: Confirm in the stripe-node 23 / endive changelog or the SDK types whether `payment_method_types` on Checkout Session create is actually removed. If it is not, restore `["card"]`.
Add a `payment_status === 'paid'` guard in `src/app/api/stripe/webhook/route.ts` and handle `async_payment_succeeded`, or keep the payment methods to card only.
Check that the Stripe dashboard webhook endpoint's API version matches `2026-09-30.endive`, then replay a signed `checkout.session.completed` event with the Stripe CLI.
Run one test-mode checkout end to end and call the price-info route against the endive version.
